thread:
sam: Hey team — hitting confusing timeout behavior with the Python SDK when doing long streaming generations. I set a long read timeout but the stream still cuts after ~60s. Anyone know which timeout wins?

rachel: Which SDK version and how are you setting the timeout (env var vs client arg)? Can you paste a tiny repro?

sam: Using redwood-inference==0.7.2. I tried both env var and client arg. Repro script below (very simplified):

sam: ```py
from redwood_inference import Client
import os
os.environ['REDWOOD_TIMEOUT'] = '120'  # seconds, tried 300 too
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('KEY'), timeout={'connect':5,'read':300})
with client.stream("gpt-lite", prompt="generate a long essay...", stream=True) as s:
    for chunk in s:
        print(chunk.text)
```

sam: But after ~60s the stream stops with: `requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: Stream read timed out` (stack trace points to httpx/_content.py).

devx-liz: Two likely things: 1) the SDK separates the initial request timeout vs per-chunk stream read timeout; 2) env var vs client arg precedence has historically been inverted in 0.7.2 for streaming. Can you paste pip freeze and any proxy/ingress config?

sam: pip freeze: `redwood-inference==0.7.2\nhttpx==0.23.3\nurllib3==1.26.16`
No proxy. TCP logs show no connection drops.

rachel: Quick workaround: try passing an explicit stream timeout param in the stream call (if available) or disable chunk-level cutoff. Eg: `client.stream(..., stream_timeout=600)` or `client = Client(..., timeout={'connect':5,'read':300,'stream':600})`. Not all keys were respected in 0.7.2.

sam: I tried `stream_timeout` on the call and it didn't change behavior. Looks like the SDK used httpx timeouts for the initial response but a separate internal watchdog kills long-chunk idle.

devx-liz: Can you reproduce with a non-streaming long generation (get all output in one response) to confirm it's stream-specific? Also add `REDWOOD_LOG=debug` and paste the portion around the failure.

sam: Non-streaming long gen works fine (just slower). Debug logs show repeated keep-alive but then `chunk read exceeded 60s -> raise ReadTimeout`.

support-bot: Created internal ticket INF-3456 and linked logs. Tagging eng-runtime for potential precedence/regression.

eng-tyler: Thanks — we tracked this down. Root cause: in 0.7.2 the `timeout` dict client arg was applied to the initial request but the streaming iterator used a hardcoded per-chunk idle cutoff (60s) that ignored `timeout['stream']`. Also env var parsing had lower precedence than client arg for a short window. We have a patch that: 1) makes client args win over env vars consistently; 2) exposes `stream`/`chunk` timeout; 3) raises a clearer exception when chunk cutoff triggers. Fix targeted in 0.7.3.

eng-tyler: Short-term workarounds: upgrade to 0.7.3 once available, or add a small keepalive activity by injecting whitespace progress every 30s from the generator side (if you control the model). If you can't upgrade, try increasing underlying httpx timeouts and set `stream=True` with `client.stream(..., stream_timeout=600)` — but note 0.7.2 may not respect that.

rachel: For our support repro steps, sam — can you run this command and paste output to the ticket?
sam: ```bash
# reproduce minimal: will time out in current 0.7.2
python -c "from redwood_inference import Client; import os; c=Client(timeout={'connect':5,'read':300});\nfor x in c.stream('gpt-lite', 'long prompt', stream=True):\n  print('.', end='', flush=True)\n"
```

sam: Added output to INF-3456. Thanks for the quick triage.

devx-liz: Filed a docs issue to clarify timeout precedence and add examples for long streaming gens. We'll update SDK changelog when 0.7.3 lands. :thumbsup:

sam: Great — will hold off on hacks and wait for 0.7.3, thanks everyone!
